faqs.question: Everyone in my Simpsonville subdivision seems to replace their AC around the same time. Why?
faqs.answer: Because the systems were installed together and aged together. Builder equipment across a subdivision shares vintage, brand, and duty cycle, so failures cluster. Your unit's documented condition still decides its own timeline, but neighborhood patterns are fair warning to get it inspected before your July.

faqs.question: Will zoning fix our hot upstairs or do we need a second system?
faqs.answer: Zoning solves it for most two-story homes at a fraction of a second system's cost. Dampers and per-floor thermostats direct cooling where the load is. A second system enters the conversation only when the diagnostic shows capacity itself is short.

faqs.question: Is a whole-home generator overkill for a suburban Simpsonville house?
faqs.answer: That depends on what an outage costs you, so the estimate prices two tiers. Essential-circuit coverage keeps refrigeration, some lights, and the furnace running affordably; whole-home coverage adds cooling and everything else.

faqs.question: What actually causes a drain to clog?
faqs.answer: Something structural that clearing punches through but never removes: a bellied section holding waste, root intrusion at a joint, or buildup narrowing the pipe. A camera inspection shows which one and exactly where.
